name: Kaltenbach
kurzbeschreibung: Starting point for the ski and glacier world Zillertal 3000 – a modern ski area with year-round snow fun.
beschreibung:
Overview

Kaltenbach is situated at an elevation of 558 metres in the heart of Tyrol's Zillertal Valley in the district of Schwaz, positioned on the western bank of the Ziller river directly opposite its sister community of Stumm. Home to around 1,330 residents, this traditional holiday resort serves as the bustling commercial anchor of the First Holiday Region in the Zillertal. The town gained international prestige as the valley hub of the multi-award-winning ski arena "Ski-optimal Hochzillertal-Kaltenbach", seamlessly connected to Hochfügen with over 90 kilometres of pistes rising up to 2,400 metres, famed for its world-class mountain gastronomy. In addition, Kaltenbach provides prime access to the magnificent Zillertal High Alpine Road, one of Austria's premier scenic mountain routes, effortlessly uniting elite alpine sports and authentic Tyrolean hospitality.

History

The settlement was first documented in 1150, its name deriving from the chilly, crystal-clear alpine waters of the torrent cascading into the valley floor. For centuries, Kaltenbach fell under the territorial jurisdiction of the Prince-Archbishops of Salzburg until the Zillertal permanently became part of Tyrol in 1816. The town's early economy was intertwined with regional silver and copper mining as well as gold deposits on nearby Mount Hainzenberg. The architectural landmark of the village centre is the Chapel of the Visitation (Marienkapelle): Erected between 1946 and 1948, it fulfilled a solemn community vow after Kaltenbach miraculously escaped major devastation during an Allied bombing run in 1944. The chapel houses an ornate early-Baroque high altar dating to around 1640. Transportation modernization accelerated with the grand opening of the narrow-gauge Zillertal Railway in 1902.

Getting There

Kaltenbach enjoys seamless transport connectivity. Motorists arrive via the Inntal Motorway A12 taking the Wiesing/Zillertal exit, following the well-maintained B169 Zillertal federal road for 15 kilometres directly to Kaltenbach, where expansive covered parking facilities await at the gondola valley terminals. Rail travellers arrive at the major rail hub of Jenbach, transferring directly on the same platform to the historic Zillertal Railway. Trains run every 30 minutes to Kaltenbach-Stumm station, situated just a brief, easy stroll from both the town center and the ski lifts.

Tips

In winter, skiing at Ski-optimal Hochzillertal is an extraordinary experience, complemented by gourmet dining at the world-renowned Kristallhütte (2,147 m) and Wedelhütte (2,350 m)—home to the highest subterranean rock wine vault in the Alps. In summer, drive the spectacular 48-kilometre Zillertal High Alpine Road up to 2,020 metres, stopping at Murmelland Zillertal at the Kaltenbacher Skihütte to view live marmots and play areas. A serene nature hike leads from the village centre up to the roaring Kaltenbach Waterfall and the adjacent Outdoor Adventure High Ropes Park. Families also appreciate the nearby Aufenfeld leisure resort featuring swimming lakes and indoor climbing.
